cohesion: All three are open slices of Epic 6 (carried debt); none blocks the other; each has real spec content (T3/T5 carry genuine design calls), which is why they warrant a batch spec rather than quickfixes.

features.title: Bound the slug quantifier in plan-store.mjs — refuse over-long slug with a named error, not an ENAMETOOLONG crash at write time
features.done_record: assertSafeSlug rejects an over-length slug with a clean named error BEFORE any path construction
edge_tests: slug exceeding max length -> named length error (never reaches fs / ENAMETOOLONG)
slug at exact max length -> accepted
existing SLUG_RE charset/traversal rejections still hold (REJECT never normalize)
features.wiring_test: plan-store write path invokes assertSafeSlug and surfaces the named error to the caller

features.title: Generators stamp a derived 'do-not-edit' header so a hand-edit is visibly wrong
features.done_record: generated files carry a derived header that makes a hand-edit detectable, WITHOUT breaking the byte-equality contract on the constitution mirrors (whose live files are the sources)
edge_tests: a hand-edited generated file is detectable as drifted via the header
constitution mirrors do NOT carry a false do-not-edit banner (their live file IS the source)
audit-baseline still passes byte-equality on the mirrors
features.wiring_test: generator emits the header; audit detects a stripped/edited header
features.design_call: The header collides with the byte-equality contracts on the constitution mirrors. The load-bearing spec decision is WHICH generated files get the header and HOW the mirror exception is expressed — this is the work, not a mechanical stamp.

features.title: Declare a release model in project.json (cicd/branch/trigger/cycle/consumer-cadence) and teach standup to read it
features.done_record: project.json declares a `release` block; standup's gather surfaces it and the main-context recommendation becomes release-model-aware (answers 'can this unreleased pile ship?')
edge_tests: standup reads the release block and selects the right regime (continuous/on-push vs on-tag/rare)
missing release block -> standup degrades gracefully, names the gap (never throws)
on-tag/rare regime -> recommendation gates on completeness (refuses to recommend cutting while a feature is half-wired)
features.wiring_test: standup gather.mjs surfaces release config; the recommendation consumer reads it in main context (Article II — helper gathers, main context decides)
features.design_call: Config schema design (five knobs, user-specified verbatim in backlog -a4f2) + the completeness_gate sub-block; keep the recommendation judgment in main context per Article II.

excluded.reason: Conditional on a THIRD caller of the slug validator appearing (Art. VI.4 abstracts at third use). Roadmap: REJECT-never-normalize, do NOT consolidate via canonicalSlug. Not a clean batch member until the third use exists.
Memory-system redesign — roadmap says it needs its own intake-to-approve cycle, do not fold into a batch.
